newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: FIGURE SKATING-LIPINSKI ON COURSE TO BE YOUNGEST CHAMPION.
newsitem.headline: FIGURE SKATING-LIPINSKI ON COURSE TO BE YOUNGEST CHAMPION.

text.p: Tara Lipinski will become the youngest world figure skating champion -- younger even than the great Sonia Henie -- if she captures the title on Saturday.
Lipinski will be 32 days younger than the Norwegian was when she won the first of her 10 successive titles back in 1927.
The petite American will be champion at 14 years, nine months and 12 days if she can hold the lead she established in Friday's short programme.

The girl from Sugar Land, Texas, who now lives in Detroit and trains there with Richard Callaghan, is in pole position with her immediate challengers not the sort of names to strike terror into her heart.

Second-placed Vanessa Gusmeroli could finish only sixth at the European championships in January while Maria Butyrskaya of Russia has won only one medal in an international championship -- she was third in the 1995 European event.
Title-holder Michelle Kwan, whom Lipinski relieved of the U.S. National and Champions Series title in the past month, is in fourth position with her confidence still not fully restored.
Even if Kwan were to produce the quality of performance that earned her last year's title, she would still need another skater to beat Lipinski before she could win.
China's Chen Lu, a close second in a spectacular battle with Kwan last year, has been off form after four months away with a foot injury and failed to qualify for the final.
Lipinski insisted she was not thinking of winning. "I think if I thought I could win it would put too much pressure on me," she said.
"I just want to skate another clean programme. To place in the medals would be nice but I'd be happy with fourth or fifth."
The dance title went on Friday to Olympic champions Oksana Gritschuk and Evgeny Platov of Russia for the fourth successive year.

Their programme blending a spectacular interpretation of Arab culture with the special demands of ice dancing earned them victory over team mates Anjelika Krylova and Oleg Ovsiannikov. Canadians Shae-Lynn Bourne and Victor Kraatz were third.
